column1: # carries.tsv -- what the `bashified` branch carries, and from where.
# ONE HOME, the bin/lib/labels.tsv shape: read at the point of use, never
# retyped. This table used to live inside bin/carry-drift.sh as a CARRIES
# heredoc, so a guard owned a data structure that outlived it --
# bin/tests/propagation.test.sh reads this mapping to answer "which script
# backs verb <v>", which is a question about the repo, not about that guard.
# carry-drift.sh was deleted 2026-08-22 (#511); the table it held
# Columns:  carried path (on bashified)  TAB  source path (on main)
# A left column under bin/ with no extension is a VERB: its bare name is what
# answered.sh is a FEEDER; the predicate it feeds is answered.jq. Carried
# without it, issue_answered() finds no predicate and returns BLIND for every
# issue -- which would take `etiquette` to exit 6 estate-wide (#568).
# HOST TOOLS, under libexec/ so nothing reads them as verbs. These are the
# (bin/lib/propagation-set.sh) -- "or ausculte is BLIND about them on a host".
# Carrying them puts them IN THE BUILD, which cut-verb-build.sh copies whole
# ("THE WHOLE bashified TREE"), so install-verb-build.sh --link can install
# them on the 05:53 tick instead of waiting for a human to run
# ONLY THE PROBES, deliberately. The provisioning half of prop_host_tools
# is NOT carried: those run when a human provisions, not on a clock, and two
# of them -- selfdev-release-tick.sh and install-verb-build.sh -- would be
# overwriting themselves mid-run. The install below is atomic anyway, but the
# smallest correct set is the one that was actually going stale.
# vault-spool-drain.sh is not a probe: it is the privileged half of `consigne`
# once the vault's read door is shut (#742), and /etc/cron.d/vault-spool-drain
# invokes it by its libexec path. It rides for the same reason the probes do --
# a host tool that only a human refreshes is a host tool that goes stale, and
# here staleness means deposits queue forever in a spool nobody can list.
# THE OUTSIDE OBSERVER, NOT a libexec/ row (#834): libexec/ installs by basename
# twice over, and this one is REPO-SHAPED -- flattened it is #826 again.
